summary: First Watch Mountain lookout site: 1933 L-4 ground cab, cabin 1940, gone in the 1960s; the 1963 tower that replaced it is a separate record.

facts.design: L-4 ground cab, cabin added in 1940
facts.status_note: Gone in the 1960s according to the FFLOS register; TrailChick says the site was replaced in 1963 by the current DNR tower

access.note: No source describes public access to the first site. Routes to Watch Mountain cross private timber land with gates and no-trespassing signs (TrailChick); a 2003 visitor walked past three locked gates to reach the 1963 tower (NHLR)

visit.trail_note: No structure to climb at the first site. The approach to the 1963 tower is the only route the sources describe in detail

events.note: L-4 ground cab built by the state (FFLOS says SDF/DNR) on the east ridge, about two miles from the current tower; FireLookout.com and TrailChick give the same year
TrailChick says Charles Boyer and Irma Huntington staffed the first lookout during their first year of marriage
Cabin added to the first lookout

July 29, 1955 Daily Chronicle item says the U.S. Forestry Service activated two lookouts as ground observer posts and that Watch Mountain was manned by James E. Grafton; an August 9, 1955 item spells the name Crafton. Both predate the 1963 tower
TrailChick says the site was replaced in 1963 by the current tower on the western side of the ridge; NHLR gives 1963 for that tower
Date registered March 17, 2011, FFLOS US 860; nominated by Irene Potter

corrections.current: NHLR US 552, WA 53; FFLOS US 860, WA 55
corrections.why: NHLR US 552 describes the standing 1963 DNR tower about a mile or two west, which has its own record (us-wa-watch-mountain). It is not this gone site.

corrections.proposed: remove this event from this record
corrections.why: The NHLR registration of February 12, 2004 is for the standing 1963 tower, not the first lookout site.
The current values are the NHLR coordinates for the standing 1963 tower. FFLOS US 860 gives 46.570700, -121.962867 for this site.
FFLOS US 860 gives 4,664 ft (1,422 m). The 1,401 m figure is the NHLR entry for the standing tower (4,595 ft).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the newer lookout is about a mile to the west; TrailChick says approximately two miles and Washington Lookouts says a little under two miles west. The story reports both figures.
The July 1955 Daily Chronicle item spells the keeper's name Grafton; the August 1955 item spells it Crafton. The story notes the difference rather than choosing one.
FFLOS and NHLR describe an L-4 cab; TrailChick and Washington Lookouts call the first lookout an L-4 ground house. The story uses cab, the register's term.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record for this id mixes in NHLR US 552, the standing 1963 DNR tower already covered by us-wa-watch-mountain: its registers, the 2004 event, coordinates and elevation are that tower's values, so corrections are proposed above. The 1955 items predate the 1963 tower, so they are read as describing the first site; that is an inference from the page's chronology. The 1967 and 1969 keepers belong to the 1963 tower and are left out. The 1938 staffing rests on TrailChick alone. The distance between the sites and the design term (cab vs ground house) conflict across sources. The 'old helipad' line on TrailChick is ambiguous and is not attributed to the first site.
